items.description: R1: track_build.py follows a green build into the Argo CD deploy it triggers — "wait until the deploy the green build triggers has rolled" — generic for every Argo-deployed repo, not KubeCoder-only. After a green build that printed a pin line (JenkinsPipelineUtils vars/cicd.groovy:133, the pin line of every writeVersionPins caller), the tracker returns only once every Application touched by that handoff has rolled the pinned commit or a descendant, and its summary reports each app. The pin line's owner, masked as `****` in the console (KubeCoder/Build-Main #551), does not stop the follow.
items.rationale: _HANDOFF_RE never captures the owner group, so a masked `****` owner cannot block a match. _wait polls every app a pushing handoff touches until it reaches ROLLED/FAILED/MANUAL/NOT_SEEN/NOT_DONE; print_follow prints each followed app under its handoff heading, with the app's own Argo-reported state.
evidence: DockerImages kube-coder-dev-local-home/track_build.py:838-882 (_wait polls each followed app to a stop)

Live, this pass: `python3 kube-coder-dev-local-home/track_build.py KubeCoder/Build-Main --buildnr 551 --no-wait-downstream` — exit 0, `kubecoder-dev rolled — Synced at 46e0aa8, health Healthy` (AnsibleSpecs slices/032_track_build_follows_argocd_sync/test-phase/v15_kubecoder_551.log)

items.description: R2: "By default." The follow into Argo CD happens with no flag given. A command line that works today (e.g. `track_build.py KubeCoder/Build-Main --hash <sha>`, KubeCoder docs/operations/deploy-operations.md:84) now waits for the roll.
items.rationale: --follow-argocd is a BooleanOptionalAction defaulting to True, and run() calls follow_deploys whenever args.follow_argocd is true — i.e. with no flag on the command line at all.
evidence: DockerImages kube-coder-dev-local-home/track_build.py:1479-1492 (run() invokes follow_deploys under args.follow_argocd alone)
Live, this pass: the #551 rerun above passed no --follow-argocd/--no-follow-argocd flag and still printed the === Argo CD follow === section

items.area: R3 — git only from the environment's clone
items.description: R3: git questions are answered only from the deploy repo's clone in /work. If the clone isn't there, the tracker stops with a message that the repo isn't there and should be added. Per ruling D1, the stop comes with a distinct exit status (the build was green, the deploy is untracked). The message names every missing deploy repo, each with the exact `git clone` line to run now, and says to declare the repo in the environment's `.kubecoder/config.yaml` for next time.
items.rationale: _follow resolves every matched handoff's repo to /work/<repo> before anything is waited on, and returns immediately if any is missing, so one stop names them all. The message gives the exact git clone line per repo and tells the agent to declare each repo in .kubecoder/config.yaml.
evidence: DockerImages kube-coder-dev-local-home/track_build.py:793-803 (_follow: every missing clone found before any wait; early return)
DockerImages kube-coder-dev-local-home/track_build.py:1239-1251 (_follow_results: git clone line per repo + declare-in-config.yaml remark)

Live, this pass: `ElectronicsInventory/ElectronicsInventory --buildnr 255` → exit 4, `no clone in /work of: ElectronicsInventoryDeploy`, with `git clone https://github.com/pvginkel/ElectronicsInventoryDeploy.git /work/ElectronicsInventoryDeploy` (test-phase/v15_electronicsinventory_255.log)

Live, this pass: `DockerImages --buildnr 2562` → exit 4, `no clone in /work of: DnsmasqDeploy` (test-phase/v15_dockerimages_2562.log) — a fresher build than the one checked during P4 (#2548), same behaviour holds

items.description: R4: prd promotions are tracked too. Every green Promote-PRD run, the record-only re-run included, prints a handoff line naming pvginkel/KubeCoderDeploy, the commit and the `prd` branch, in a form that shows whether the run moved `prd`. Today the job prints none: KubeCoderDeploy Jenkinsfile.promote:98, :100, :129. Pointed at a promotion that moved `prd`, the tracker follows the Applications that track `prd` (kubecoder-prd) to the promoted commit.
items.rationale: Jenkinsfile.promote now prints exactly one of the two forms once prd names the commit (after 'Advancing prd', before 'Recording the release'). Both forms fit _HANDOFF_RE's pushed/already groups, distinct from the pin line's pins group and from the job's other echoes. The mechanism is proven offline and by the tracker's unit suite; the end-to-end live run is a real Promote-PRD execution, which is owed to the operator (V16) since promotion is run by hand.
evidence: KubeCoderDeploy Jenkinsfile.promote:134-141 (the two forms, printed once prd names the commit)
DockerImages kube-coder-dev-local-home/track_build.py:122-127 (_HANDOFF_RE parses both promote forms via the pushed/already groups)
KubeCoderDeploy 35e1f81 code-reviewer signoff (phases/P1, live promote line witnessed on Promote-PRD #9, per state.json history phase 1 round 1)

items.description: R5: when none of the tracked green builds prints a handoff line, the tracker says so, in words that tell the agent it may have to fix a pipeline for the tracker to follow the Argo CD deployment. It then exits with the build's own result, not a failure.
items.rationale: print_follow's no-handoffs branch names the two known handoff shapes and says the pipeline may need a fix before the tracker can follow the deployment. FollowReport.exit_status returns 0 in this case (no error, no missing clones, no followed states), so the exit stays the build's own result.

items.description: R6: the default `--appear-timeout` is 5 minutes, up from 30 s (DockerImages kube-coder-dev-local-home/track_build.py:366-371), and the help text agrees.
items.rationale: --appear-timeout now defaults to 300.0 seconds, and its help text reads exactly '(default: 300, 5 minutes)'.

items.description: Only the Applications that roll the handoff are waited on: those whose source repoURL and targetRevision match the pushed repo and branch, and, for a pin line, whose helm valueFiles name a pinned file, in either the `../config/<stage>/values.yaml` form or the `$values/config/<stage>/values.yaml` form. A KubeCoder/Build-Main pin commit waits on kubecoder-dev and not on kubecoder-prd, which tracks `prd`. A dev-only pin to a repo whose dev and prd apps share `main` (keycloak's shape) waits on the dev app only. A three-source upstream-chart app is matched through its `ref: values` source.
items.rationale: _tracks matches repoURL+targetRevision; value_files resolves both the relative and the $ref forms and matching_sources additionally requires a values-file overlap only when the handoff names files (a pin line) — a handoff naming no files (promote, already-carries) matches every app on the repo+branch regardless of valueFiles.
evidence: Live, this pass: the #551 rerun waited on kubecoder-dev only, not kubecoder-prd, over the real 50-Application estate (test-phase/v15_kubecoder_551.log)

items.description: For a handoff that pushed a new commit, the tracker does not declare an app rolled on the strength of Argo's compared revision alone. An app that is OutOfSync at the new commit, with its previous operation finished, is still waited on. An app that Argo reports Synced at the commit or a descendant, with no operation running and health not Progressing, is done even when the commit rendered no change and so no new operation ran.
items.rationale: app_state's docstring and body implement exactly this: an app not yet compared at (or past) sha is UNSEEN/ROLLING regardless of operation state; once compared at/past sha, ROLLED requires Synced with no running sync and health not Progressing — reached whether or not a new operation ran.
evidence: Live, this pass: kubecoder-dev reported 'Synced at 46e0aa8, health Healthy' for #551 — Synced at/past the commit, no sync running, health Healthy — rolled (test-phase/v15_kubecoder_551.log)

items.description: The tracker stops, with a message saying what happened, rather than waiting indefinitely when: Argo CD does not pick up the commit within a deadline (push-only sync, a lost webhook); the roll is not done by the roll deadline; an app carries a SyncError condition; an app has no automated sync policy (today argocd-prd); or a handoff matches no Application. The script's exit-status documentation covers every outcome it can end with.
items.rationale: _wait bounds both deadlines (pickup → NOT_SEEN, roll → NOT_DONE), routes any app without automated sync straight to MANUAL, and app_state routes any *Error condition to FAILED. A handoff no Application matches is logged and appended to report.unmatched, never waited on. The module docstring enumerates exit statuses 0/1/3/4/5/6/7 and their precedence.
evidence: DockerImages kube-coder-dev-local-home/track_build.py:784-788 (unmatched handoff logged, not waited on)

items.description: When a followed app's sync fails, ends unhealthy, stops on a SyncError, or is not done at the roll deadline, the tracker saves into `--log-dir`, beside failing builds' console logs, the operation message, the conditions, the failed or unhealthy resources, and the app's `tf-presync-<app>` hook Job log from argocd-hooks. The summary names the saved file.
items.rationale: diagnosis() assembles exactly these sections (operation, conditions, resources the sync failed, live resources not healthy via _unhealthy_lines, the tf-presync-<app> hook Job via _hook_lines); save_diagnosis writes it under --log-dir, and print_follow prints '↳ diagnosis: <path>' under the app's summary line.

items.description: The tracker reads Argo CD state from the Kubernetes API with the environment's default `~/.kube/config`. It runs under the dev container's system python3, without kubectl or the iac sidecar, and writes nothing to Argo CD or the cluster.
items.rationale: Kube reads ~/.kube/config context 'prd' directly via urllib and PyYAML; every Kube method (get/items/log/applications/application) issues a plain GET, with no PATCH/POST/PUT anywhere in the file. No subprocess call to kubectl exists; the only subprocess use is Clone._git, itself read-only (fetch, rev-parse, cat-file, merge-base).
evidence: Full read of track_build.py this pass found no write verb (PATCH/POST/PUT/DELETE) and no kubectl invocation anywhere in the file
Live, this pass: all three reruns executed under this container's system python3 (no kubectl on PATH here), confirming the runtime claim

items.description: Ruling F1: the roll wait is bounded. It has a roll deadline, default 10 minutes and overridable by a flag. After it, the tracker stops with its own exit status, names every app still Progressing, and saves the same evidence as a failed roll.
items.rationale: --roll-timeout defaults to 600.0 seconds ('10 minutes') and is a plain float flag, so it is overridable. _wait counts it from f.seen_at (the first poll where Argo CD showed the app past UNSEEN), moving an app to NOT_DONE once exceeded, and save_diagnosis runs for NOT_DONE exactly as for FAILED.
evidence: DockerImages kube-coder-dev-local-home/track_build.py:861-864, :872-874 (NOT_DONE from seen_at + roll_timeout; diagnosis saved)

items.description: Ruling F1: a handoff that pushed no new deploy commit has no new sync to wait for. That covers "already carries these pins" (JenkinsPipelineUtils vars/cicd.groovy:114) and a Promote-PRD re-run that only records a release tag (KubeCoderDeploy Jenkinsfile.promote:77-82). The tracker reports each matched app's current sync and health state and returns, rather than waiting on health, even when Argo reports the app Progressing. For "already carries", the state is read against the branch's current head.
items.rationale: _follow marks every Followed whose handoff.pushed is False as CURRENT immediately and logs its current state; _wait is only ever called with the subset whose handoff.pushed is True, so a pushed-nothing handoff's apps are never polled or waited on regardless of their health. report.commits reads the branch head from the clone (handoff.sha or clone.head(branch)) precisely for the sha-less 'already carries' case.
evidence: DockerImages kube-coder-dev-local-home/track_build.py:807-809 (commits: sha or branch head from the clone)
DockerImages kube-coder-dev-local-home/track_build.py:822-828 (CURRENT for pushed=False; _wait called on pushed-only subset)
